section_summary: The section concludes a draft Japanese constitution, covering civil rights, the Diet, Cabinet, judiciary, finance, local government, amendments, and transitional provisions. The remaining documents trace State Department and Far Eastern Commission debate over reviewing the constitution, consulting SCAP, and deciding whether the Japanese Diet had fulfilled its review obligation.

subfiles.title: Draft Japanese Constitution, Articles XIV–XCV
subfiles.about: The concluding articles set out rights, national and local institutions, amendment rules, and transitional provisions.
subfiles.summary: These pages continue a draft constitution begun before this section. They guarantee political, religious, labor, property, and criminal procedure rights; establish the Diet, Cabinet, courts, fiscal controls, and local self-government; and prescribe amendment, supremacy, and transitional rules.

subfiles.title: Consultative Message to SCAP on Review of the Japanese Constitution
subfiles.about: The Acting Legal Adviser recommends U.S. cooperation in drafting a Far Eastern Commission request for SCAP’s views.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum argues that the United States should help draft the consultative message and seek SCAP’s evidence on how the constitution works. It warns that opposing or vetoing the request would alienate other Commission members and hinder a prompt, quiet review.

subfiles.title: Draft of Message to General MacArthur
subfiles.about: The Commission requests information on Japan’s constitutional review and the constitution’s operation.
subfiles.summary: Requests an update on the Japanese review, practical experience, and the Supreme Commander’s comments.

subfiles.title: Review of the Japanese Constitution
subfiles.from: Walter Wilds, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Occupied Areas
subfiles.to: United States member, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: The U.S. member is authorized to seek a revision to the proposed consultative message.
subfiles.summary: Seeks reference to the Potsdam Declaration and other controlling documents, while permitting acceptance of the original draft.

subfiles.title: Review of the Japanese Constitution by the Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.about: Allison objects to authorizing a proposed Commission message to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Citing agreed U.S. policy for a prompt, inconspicuous review, Allison opposes transmitting the draft message.

subfiles.title: Proposed Instructions for U.S. Member on Review of Japanese Constitution
subfiles.about: Dunning proposes treating the Japanese Diet’s actions as satisfying the required constitutional review.
subfiles.summary: After SCAP’s reply, Dunning anticipates questions about whether the Diet complied with the Far Eastern Commission’s review policy. She recommends a firm U.S. position that it did, arguing that pressure for further action could create political instability and prolong Commission debate.

subfiles.title: Telephone Conversation with Mr. Bullock on Review of Japanese Constitution
subfiles.about: An Australian Embassy official discusses further Diet review and possible Commission communication with SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Bullock says Australia opposes Allied changes to the constitution but favors encouraging the Diet committee to meet and considering another consultative message. Dunning disagrees with further messages and recommends a final U.S. position that the Diet has fulfilled its review obligation.
